issue.title: Do not remove legacy watcher templates in 7.x

labels.name: Team:Data Management (obsolete)
labels.description: DO NOT USE. This team no longer exists.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Some previous 7.x release validate that these legacy templates exist in
the cluster (the validation executes on non-master nodes too). This can
cause the rolling upgrade test (particulary the ones that do not upgrade
the entire cluster ie. mixed cluster scenarios) to hang waiting for
watcher to be started, however it will never start because of the
legacy templates validation failing.

This is not a problem per se for "real life" rolling upgrades as this does not
block the rolling upgrades, nor does it raise any errors, it will
however stop watcher on the nodes that detect it (until the said nodes are
upgraded, at which point watcher is started).

Note that we'll have a follow up PR that'll re-enable the rolling upgrade tests

Fixes #82109

body:
Here are my raw notes to track the requirements needed for Watcher to perform a rolling upgrade such that it will pass the validation check:

tl;dr
1) revert the Watcher changes from #80937 for 7.x (its fine to keep it for 8.x)
2) ignore `.triggered_watches, .watch-history-9, .watches` templates from the deprecation info API template check 
3) change the validation logic for 8.0 to avoid this mess in the future
4) remove the extraneous templates in `x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/resources` this includes watches-11.json, triggered_watches-11.json, watcher-history-[no-ilm]-[10|11].json

### from 6.8, 7.0, 7.1, 7.2

To pass validation during a rolling upgrade to 7.17:
Requires legacy index templates named:

```
.triggered_watches
.watches
.watch-history-9
```

```java  
    public static boolean validate(ClusterState state) {
        return state.getMetaData().getTemplates().containsKey(WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.HISTORY_TEMPLATE_NAME) &&
                state.getMetaData().getTemplates().containsKey(WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.TRIGGERED_TEMPLATE_NAME) &&
                state.getMetaData().getTemplates().containsKey(WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.WATCHES_TEMPLATE_NAME);
    }
```


7.10 : https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/7.10/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/watcher/support/WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.java


### from 7.11, 7.12, 7.13, 7.14, 7.15, 7.16, 7.17

To pass validation during a rolling upgrade to 7.17:
Requires either legacy or composable index template named `.watcher-history-*`

```java  
    public static boolean validate(ClusterState state) {
        // A .watch-history should exist, whether it is a legacy or composable index template
        // that doesn't matter when deciding to start watcher.
        final Stream<String> watcherHistoryTemplateIds = Stream.concat(state.getMetadata().templatesV2().keySet().stream(),
            Arrays.stream(state.getMetadata().getTemplates().keys().toArray(String.class)));
        return watcherHistoryTemplateIds.filter(s -> s.startsWith(".watch-history-"))
            .map
            (s -> Integer.valueOf(s.substring(s.lastIndexOf('-') + 1)))
            .anyMatch(version -> version >= 9);
    }

```

So to pass validation for any 7.x to rolling upgrade to 7.17 the min required templates are:
```
.triggered_watches (legacy)
.watches (legacy)
.watch-history-9 (legacy)
.watch-history-10 (legacy)
.watch-history-11 (legacy)
.watch-history-12 (composable)
```

In all cases the elder version will land the necessary templates and once #80937 is reverted nothing is explicitly deleting these. However, starting in 7.13 the .watches and .triggered_watches are now system indices and no longer installed by default and fortunately starting with 7.11 we only care about the .watcher-history-* which is still there

However, this is complicated by the fact that the following templates  _may_ still use the the "doc" type. 

```
 .triggered_watches, .watch-history-9, .watches
 ```

Both .watches and .triggered watch templates when originally installed with 6.8 or early 7.x will still carry "doc" triggering a deprecation warning from the deprecation info API. .watch-history-9 which is still needed for validation with some versions are also required but will also trigger the deprecation warning. We _could_ re-introduce these templates as dummy templates to allow the validation to pass or we can simply ignore these unused templates via the deprecation warning check (they are no longer used, but can not be deleted due to the validation requirement)

### from 7.17 to 8.0

To pass validation during a rolling upgrade to 8.0:
Requires ONE of the following composable templates
```
.watch-history-12
.watch-history-no-ilm-12
.watch-history-13
.watch-history-no-ilm-13
.watch-history-14
.watch-history-no-ilm-14
```

```java 

        return state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.HISTORY_TEMPLATE_NAME) ||
            state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(WatcherIndexTemplateRegistryField.HISTORY_TEMPLATE_NAME_NO_ILM) ||
            // Template versions 12 or 13 are also ok to have (no breaking changes). At some point these will be upgraded to version 14.
            state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(".watch-history-12") ||
            state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(".watch-history-no-ilm-12") ||
            state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(".watch-history-13") ||
            state.getMetadata().templatesV2().containsKey(".watch-history-no-ilm-13");
```

issue.title: Prevent watcher from failing to start if its templates are missing

labels.name: Team:Data Management (obsolete)
labels.description: DO NOT USE. This team no longer exists.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This commit prevents watcher from failing to start if its templates are unavailable. Previously the watcher service
would fail to start if (for example) the `.watch-history-14` template did not exist. This could happen during a rolling
upgrade. In that case, the watcher service would fail to start even though it could reasonably keep writing without its
templates.

issue.title: Watcher history created as index with wrong mapping instead of data stream after 8.0 upgrade

labels.name: Team:Data Management (obsolete)
labels.description: DO NOT USE. This team no longer exists.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.0.1

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Elastic Cloud

### Problem Description

After upgrading from 7.17 to 8.0.1 we noticed that some watches would not write their history.
The ES logs has many log lines similar to
`[instance-0000000115] watch history could not be written [mywatch_5a0585ef-b8b1-4526-8b24-9fb9bf58981d-2022-03-15T11:29:32.801579308Z], failure [org.elasticsearch.index.mapper.MapperParsingException: failed to parse]`

I noticed that `.watcher-history-16` has the wrong mapping as everything just has default `.text`+`.keyword`, and the index template has a lot more specific fields. But the index template applies to a data stream, but `.watcher-history-16` got created as an index, so the template didn't apply. It should have been created as a data stream after https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/64252, but somehow it didn't.




### Steps to Reproduce

(unconfirmed)
Create a 7.17 cluster with multiple nodes
Create multiple watches that fire rapidly.
Upgrade ES to 8.x
`.watcher-history-16` should be created as data stream, but got created as an index.

I tried it with a simple cluster and one watch firing every second and it upgraded to datastream, so it might be a race condition or depend on how many watches/how many nodes (we have ~80 watches/12 nodes)

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

This looks a bit similar to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/56732 except now that it's a data stream it won't be "fixed" by waiting until roll over.
